Hi,

I have a question regarding the use of the Z-test to compare density
estimates in different strata and was hoping someone might be able to
help me out. I used line transects to estimate ungulate densities in a
reserve in southern India. I had transects in two different strata
(habitat types). Data from both strata were pooled together to obtain
the detection function (to overcome problems of low sample sizes in one
of the strata) & density subsequently estimated independently for each
strata.
In this case, can the Z statistic still be calculated as
z = D1 - D2 / sqrt(sqr(SE1)+sqr(SE2))
- as in page 381 of the DISTANCE SAMPLING GUIDE. Given that the
estimates are not necessarily independent, is this valid? If not, how
does one need to modify it?

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Regards,
Mahesh Sankaran
Dept. of Biology,
Syracuse University,
Syracuse, NY 13244

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Z-test
parts:
> > I have a question regarding the use of the Z-test to compare density
> > estimates in different strata and was hoping someone might be able to
> > help me out. I used line transects to estimate ungulate densities in a
> > reserve in southern India. I had transects in two different strata
> > (habitat types). Data from both strata were pooled together to obtain
> > the detection function (to overcome problems of low sample sizes in one
> > of the strata) & density subsequently estimated independently for each
> > strata.
> > In this case, can the Z statistic still be calculated as
> > z = D1 - D2 / sqrt(sqr(SE1)+sqr(SE2))
> > - as in page 381 of the DISTANCE SAMPLING GUIDE. Given that the
> > estimates are not necessarily independent, is this valid? If not, how
> > does one need to modify it?

You need to first find the variance of D1/f(0) and of D2/f(0) -
i.e. variance of n_1/L_1 and of variance n_2/L_2 if you don't have
clusters. If you have clusters, variance of n_1 . E^(s)/L_1 is found by
the delta method. Variance of (D1-D2)/f(0) is then the sum of these
variances. Now find variance of [(D1-D2)/f(0)]*f(0) = D1-D2 by the delta
method. z = (D1-D2)/sqrt[var(D1-D2)]

Similar calculations but in a stratified context are shown on pp388-390 of
the book.

Steve Buckland
